description: Committee recommends approving Affordable Housing Strategy 2025-2030 in principle.
Approval subject to future budget allocations.
Strategy aims to diversify housing and increase affordable supply.
Also recommends receiving Housing Needs Assessment 2024.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Tribal Chief Arcand urged municipal financial investment to leverage other government funding.
The Housing Needs Assessment 2024 is Saskatoon's first comprehensive analysis.
Mayor Block questioned how the city determines the right funding targets for housing needs.
80% of individuals experiencing homelessness identify as Indigenous.

segments.title: City administration presents housing strategy
segments.takeaway: Administration presented Saskatoon's first housing needs assessment and the new housing strategy, seeking approval in principle subject to future budget allocations.

segments.title: Public comments: Tribal Chief Mark Arcand
segments.takeaway: Tribal Chief Mark Arcand emphasized the need for proper investments from all levels of government to address the affordable housing crisis and support vulnerable populations.

segments.title: Public comments: Rachel Stinky, Saskatoon Community Foundation
segments.takeaway: Rachel Stinky highlighted the high cost of inaction on affordable housing and committed the Saskatoon Community Foundation to being a strong partner in finding solutions.

segments.title: Public comments: Gord Taylor, Salvation Army
segments.takeaway: Gord Taylor emphasized the need to address the entire housing continuum, including a year-round basic shelter, to ensure people are prepared and supported to stay housed.

segments.title: Public comments: Ron Klauson, Salvation Army
segments.takeaway: Ron Klauson proposed a public-private partnership model, possibly involving tiny home communities, to address homelessness and provide stable housing with support services.

segments.title: Public comments: Angela Bishop, Campone Housing
segments.takeaway: Angela Bishop supported the strategy, emphasizing the importance of Indigenous-led housing solutions and culturally informed approaches to address disproportionate housing challenges.

segments.title: Public comments: Chris Grett, Saskatchewan Realtor Association
segments.takeaway: Chris Grett commended the strategy's targeted approach, emphasizing diversifying housing options, increasing supply, strengthening collaborations, and raising awareness of housing needs.

segments.title: Public comments: Matthew Giddette, Metis Nation Saskatchewan
segments.takeaway: Matthew Giddette supported the strategy, highlighting the urgent need for increased affordable housing, sustainable operational funding, and prioritizing Indigenous-led projects.

segments.title: Committee questions for administration
segments.takeaway: Committee members questioned administration on the housing gap, the urgency of prioritized actions, and the city's financial contributions to affordable housing initiatives.

segments.title: Committee comments and motion
segments.takeaway: Committee members offered comments, thanking speakers and administration, emphasizing the need for collaborative action and addressing funding challenges before moving the recommendations.

description: Committee recommends five-year tax abatements for 11 projects.
This supports 208 new affordable rental units.
City would forgo $1.5 million in property taxes.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Councillor Kelleher questioned incentives for larger family units.
How to incentivize larger affordable family units remains unclear.
Priority given to Indigenous organizations for affordable housing projects.
No further affordable housing incentive calls planned at this time.

description: New affordable housing incentives considered for 2025-2026 budget.
Options propose up to $5.4 million for new housing.
Could create up to 319 new affordable units by 2027.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
Proposed funding would be a service level enhancement, added by council at budget time.
Housing providers need stable annual funding for new affordable housing development.
Housing strategy prioritizes increasing affordable housing and Indigenous-led initiatives.

segments.title: Affordable Housing Budget Options Presentation
segments.takeaway: Staff presented three operating budget options and one capital budget option for affordable housing incentives, recommending Option 3 for full strategy implementation.

segments.title: Questions on Affordable Housing Budget Details
segments.takeaway: Councillors questioned the Neighborhood Land Development Fund's role, current funding, and the mill rate impact of the recommended budget option.

segments.title: Affordable Housing Report Received
segments.takeaway: The committee moved to receive the report on Affordable Housing Incentives – Budget Options as information for future budget deliberations.

description: City will not create a bylaw for residential security cameras.
Instead, it will add privacy guidelines to the Good Neighbor Guide.
These guidelines will inform residents about provincial privacy laws.

chips.text: City Solicitor explained challenges of enforcing a bylaw without a proper plan.
Delegate shared personal experience of costly legal action to address neighbor's cameras.
Privacy protection should not depend on an individual's ability to afford legal counsel.

description: City explores YMCA operating Harry Bailey Aquatic Centre.
Harry Bailey Aquatic Centre renovation reopens in 2026.
Partnership aims for accessible recreation, lower operating costs.

chips.text: Councillor confirmed no city staff positions will be lost with YMCA partnership.
Partnership aims to reduce reliance on property tax for facility operations.
YMCA Saskatoon CEO expressed interest in operating Harry Bailey Aquatic Centre.
